questions.question: When should an air supply control lever be in its "normal" position?

options.text: When changing a tire.
When applying the trailer emergency brakes.
When pulling a trailer.
When using your spring brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling a trailer.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles have tractor protection controls operated by levers instead of knobs. When an air supply control is in its "normal" position, it is set correctly for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: Older trailers have no spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, what happens?

options.text: The trailer will stop normally.
The trailer will have no brakes.
The trailer will speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air tank leaks and loses air, there will be no brakes to stop the trailer. The wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: How should you position trailers in a double or triple combination?

options.text: Spread cargo weight evenly between all trailers.
Put the heaviest trailer closest to the cab.
Put the heaviest trailer in the rear.
Trailer weight does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the heaviest trailer closest to the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be in the rear.

questions.question: How should cargo be loaded to prevent a rollover?

options.text: Place it near the front of the trailer.
Place it near the rear of the trailer.
Spread it out across the trailer.
Load most weight on the driver's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread it out across the trailer.
questions.explanation: To prevent rollover, spread cargo evenly across the trailer and keep the weight centered and as low to the ground as possible.

questions.question: What should the trailer hand valve be used for?

options.text: For parking.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Together with the brake pedal while driving.
On slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: Why should you watch the road ahead while driving?

options.text: It is safer than only watching your mirrors.
It does not improve safety.
It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous in combination vehicles. By looking ahead for obstacles, you can plan lane changes early and avoid emergency moves.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor without a trailer.
A tractor with two trailers.
A tractor that exceeds the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor operating without a trailer. These are difficult to operate and require extra caution.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: Regularly to activate brakes in all driving conditions.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid.
Only if the trailer is carrying cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve should be used only to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving because it may cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether a pre-1998 trailer has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), how can you check?

options.text: Look for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Assume the vehicle has ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes. This will tell you if the trailer has ABS.

questions.question: When a vehicle goes around a corner, what happens to the rear wheels?

options.text: They follow the same path as the front wheels.
They follow a different path than the front wheels.
They should not be a concern to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: They follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: When turning a corner, rear wheels follow a different path than front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Longer vehicles have greater off-tracking than shorter vehicles.

questions.question: How can you tell if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes. This tells you if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: What happens if a load is placed on one side of a trailer?

options.text: The trailer may lean and could roll over.
The trailer gets extra support during turns.
The brakes improve.
The steering improves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may lean and could roll over.
questions.explanation: If weight is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer may lean to one side. This increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect cause?

options.text: Trailers to roll over.
Loud noises.
Trucks to speed up.
Trucks to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trailers to roll over.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause a trailer to roll over when you change lanes. To prevent this, make lane changes slowly and safely.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.

options.text: Level with
Slightly higher than
Slightly lower than

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: When braking while pulling a trailer with anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Use extra braking force to make sure the brakes work.
Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving a tractor-trailer with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would if the vehicle did not have ABS.

questions.question: What does rearward amplification refer to?

options.text: The amount of noise at the back of a vehicle.
The cause of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
How many trailers a tractor can pull.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cause of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the "crack-the-whip" effect. This effect makes vehicles with trailers more likely to roll over.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be directly behind the cab?

options.text: The lightest trailer
The heaviest trailer
The smallest trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest trailer
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be in the back.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full semitrailers attached.

options.text: Quicker
Easier
More difficult

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no semitrailer attached. Bobtail tractors take longer to stop and require more distance than a tractor with a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: Before a trip, how do you make sure air flows to all trailers?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for escaping air.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Let air pressure build, then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching all trailers.

questions.question: When should a trolley valve be used?

options.text: While driving.
Only to test trailer brakes.
When parking uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trolley valve controls the trailer brakes and should only be used to test them. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it when parking because it may release the air pressure and let the brakes go loose.
